attributes.has_name: Case A — Tiger not detected (unusual animal pose)
attributes.malfunction_description: Analysis case A. Functional insufficiency: classifier generalization limitation. Triggering condition: unusual animal pose. Outcome: Tiger not detected. The classifier and sensing chain operate without a fault, but the learned representation does not adequately cover the pose.

attributes.has_name: Case A-SW — Tiger classification false negative (unusual animal pose)
attributes.malfunction_description: Software contribution to system Case A. With qualified fused inputs and an object hypothesis for a tiger, TigerDetectionApp produces tigerDetected=false at detectionOut throughout the required detection window for an unusual pose. The classifier executes correctly but its learned representation does not generalize sufficiently. This output insufficiency can contribute to the system missed detection unless another mechanism compensates; it is not an independent hazardous scenario or an implementation fault.

attributes.has_name: Case B — Tiger not detected (small apparent target size)
attributes.malfunction_description: Analysis case B. Functional insufficiency: limited spatial resolution. Triggering condition: small apparent target size. Outcome: Tiger not detected. The correctly operating sensor resolves too few target features for reliable recognition. The system missed-detection outcome requires insufficient complementary lidar/infrared information or another uncompensated limitation. The incoming Case D propagation covers the combined sensing-information boundary for this small-target scenario.

attributes.has_name: Case C1 — Tiger not detected (camouflage and partial concealment)
attributes.malfunction_description: The original sensor configuration used RGB and lidar. A tiger remaining still against a similar-looking background and using partial vegetation cover may present too few discriminating features for timely recognition, even when both sensors function correctly. Functional insufficiency: insufficient sensing diversity for visually concealed targets. Triggering condition: camouflage and partial concealment. Outcome: Tiger not detected. Runtime measure SOTIF_RT_001 adds thermal sensing and evaluation to address this concern in the current baseline.

attributes.has_name: Case C1-SW — Usable thermal evidence suppressed by fusion
attributes.malfunction_description: Software contribution to system Case C1 after thermal runtime measure SOTIF_RT_001. All sensor channels provide fresh, valid data. Partial occlusion and a cluttered background leave weak RGB features and ambiguous lidar geometry, while exposed target areas provide usable LWIR contrast. The intended fusion weighting or corroboration policy suppresses the thermal-supported object hypothesis because RGB/lidar support is weak. Fusion omits the candidate from objectListOut or delivers it after the required detection window. The software executes its specified policy without an implementation fault. This output insufficiency can contribute to the system missed detection unless independent use of the aligned samples or another mechanism compensates. It occurs before tiger classification; it is not the classifier generalization limitation of Case A-SW. Adequate thermal contrast is assumed here; Case C2 addresses insufficient thermal contrast.

attributes.has_name: Case C2 — Tiger not detected (low thermal contrast)
attributes.malfunction_description: Follow-up assessment of runtime measure SOTIF_RT_001, which introduced thermal sensing and evaluation to address Case C1. Functional insufficiency: limited contrast discrimination. Triggering condition: low target–background thermal contrast. Outcome: Tiger not detected. The infrared channel operates without a fault, but the intended function cannot reliably discriminate the target from its thermal background. This limits the thermal measure's effectiveness, including when camouflage and partial concealment coincide with low thermal contrast. The system missed-detection outcome is not established by low thermal contrast alone when RGB or lidar can compensate. The incoming Case D propagation covers the low-contrast scenario in which the combined observations remain insufficient.

attributes.has_name: Case D — Sensing capability insufficient for operating condition
attributes.malfunction_description: All three required channels (RGB, lidar and LWIR) acquire fresh, valid data without a hardware or implementation fault, but their combined observations contain insufficient discriminating information for the required detection performance. Assess low light combined with low thermal contrast and ambiguous lidar geometry, or rain, glare, obstruction and small apparent target size when the other modalities cannot compensate. Darkness alone is not an operating-condition violation. Unlike Case C1-SW, this case concerns information that is unavailable in the observations, not usable thermal evidence discarded by fusion. Case D can contribute to Case B in the small-target scenario, or Case C2 in the low-thermal-contrast scenario, only when complementary modalities remain insufficient. It can contribute to Case E only when the operating-condition estimator also fails to recognize the actual capability limitation. An adequate monitor can detect Case D and issue the unavailable indication; Case D alone does not imply Case E. All three channels remain required; no reduced-sensor operating mode is credited.

An actual operating-condition or combined sensing-capability limitation is not recognized within the required time because the intended estimator has insufficient sensitivity or incomplete scenario coverage, despite correct execution and functioning hardware. For the linked Case D scenario, channel reports can be fresh and syntactically valid while image quality, lidar returns or thermal contrast provide insufficient evidence of detection capability. The capability assessment nevertheless indicates acceptable operation, so the lifecycle controller receives no timely unavailable request and the operator receives no corresponding indication. The D-to-E propagation requires both the actual limitation and this estimation insufficiency; it is not an inevitable consequence of weak sensor information. Validate rain, sustained glare, aperture obstruction and the observable evidence of combined thermal limitations. A scene-level contrast estimate cannot guarantee contrast for an unseen target. Darkness within validated nighttime conditions is acceptable. Cases A/A-SW and C1-SW can occur within the operating envelope and are not automatically detectable by this monitor. An implementation fault that accepts invalid status or fails to issue a requested warning remains in the fault analyses.
